title: Two tracks to Tehran: The new efforts to stop another US-Iran war – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Geranmayeh describes two diplomatic tracks, the E4+R4 (Britain, France, Germany, Italy plus Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia) and a Pakistan-Turkey-Saudi security-chief mission to Tehran, aimed at preventing a renewed US-Iran war after Trump said 'anything's possible' post-midterms. With America absent, she sees an emerging middle-power order and urges Europe to tie sanctions relief to stronger IAEA monitoring and to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

insights.claim: Asked whether he would launch a new attack on Iran after the midterm elections, Donald Trump replied 'Anything's possible', triggering a flurry of diplomacy to prevent a return to all-out war.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Renewed US-Iran conflict is a live post-midterm risk for oil and shipping.
insights.locator: Anything's possible was Donald Trump's response

insights.claim: A return to full-scale war between America and Iran may be inevitable given Trump's zero-sum instincts and apparent desire for a hard-power legacy.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Investors should keep a meaningful probability on renewed high-intensity Gulf conflict.
insights.quote: A return to full-scale war between America and Iran may be inevitable given Trump’s zero-sum instincts and apparent desire for a hard-power legacy.

insights.claim: Tehran has signalled that its response to renewed US or Israeli strikes would be far more damaging than anything the Middle East has absorbed in the past eight months.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Escalation would likely hit regional energy infrastructure harder than in the prior conflict.

insights.claim: The Trump administration is attempting to impose a full blockade on Iran, while the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and its reopening is a central diplomatic goal.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: An ongoing Hormuz closure is a major supply shock factor for crude and LNG markets.

insights.claim: In recent weeks the Houthis have damaged critical infrastructure inside Saudi Arabia and attacked Red Sea shipping, demonstrating Iran's reach through its Yemeni ally.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Saudi energy infrastructure and Red Sea shipping face elevated disruption risk.
insights.locator: It has already shown its reach

insights.claim: A joint Houthi-Iranian effort to disrupt transit through both the straits of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb would have global economic ramifications.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Dual-chokepoint disruption is a key tail scenario for oil prices, freight rates and insurance.
insights.quote: A joint effort by the Houthis and Iran to disrupt transit through two vital waterways—the straits of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb—would have global economic ramifications.
insights.locator: It has already shown its reach

insights.claim: E4 (Britain, France, Germany, Italy) and R4 (Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia) foreign ministers met in Istanbul on October 23rd on a two-state solution, ending the US-Iran war, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and defending Saudi Arabia against a Houthi offensive.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: A new non-US diplomatic format is engaging directly on Gulf shipping security.

insights.claim: Adding Italy to the E3 bolsters European weight, offsetting Britain's Brexit-induced weakness and Germany's lost regional influence over its support for Israel; Italy also did not join last year's E3 'snapback' of Iran sanctions, which could help it reopen negotiations.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Italy may emerge as Europe's preferred interlocutor with Tehran.

insights.claim: All R4 members except Egypt signed the Mecca Defence Alliance military pact in August, and members activated its collective defence measures in response to the Houthi offensive against Saudi Arabia.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: A functioning Gulf-Turkey-Pakistan defence pact changes regional security and arms-procurement dynamics.

insights.claim: The E4 and R4 could use combined economic clout to press China to use its deep trade ties with Iran to secure a lasting reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: China is framed as a potential key to reopening Hormuz.
insights.locator: Teaming up more actively with the R4

themes.theme: Tehran track and Iran's internal politics

insights.claim: Three days after Istanbul, security chiefs from Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia met Iran's leaders in Tehran to draw Iran into a diplomatic process, which also handed Iran a PR victory.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Regional powers are hedging by engaging Tehran directly despite US maximum pressure.

insights.claim: The Islamic Republic's elite will probably remain in power for the foreseeable future, with hard-line military factions brought forward by the war now dominating decision-making.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Regime-change scenarios are unlikely; expect a harder-line Iranian negotiating posture.
insights.locator: If war and maximum pressure pushed Iran

insights.claim: If war and maximum pressure pushed Iran, a country of over 90 million, towards state collapse, the consequences for its neighbours and Europe would be disastrous, especially since neither America nor Israel is likely to fund reconstruction.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: State collapse in Iran would be a major migration, security and energy shock for Europe.
insights.locator: If war and maximum pressure pushed Iran

insights.claim: America's absence from both meetings shows European and regional powers increasingly working around an unpredictable Washington rather than with it.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Diminished US role raises the importance of European and Gulf diplomatic actors.

insights.claim: For the R4, Trump's handling of Iran has shattered the assumption that US forces offer iron-clad protection to allies, a reality Europeans also face over Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Erosion of US security guarantees supports regional defence spending and self-reliance.

insights.claim: America and Israel have the military capacity to devastate the region but have proved unable or unwilling to win the peace.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Military dominance is not producing stability; conflict risk persists.
insights.quote: America and Israel might have the military capacity to devastate the region, but they have proved unable or unwilling to win the peace.

insights.claim: Regional powers see Europe as a more reliable security, defence and economic partner than Russia, China or the US as they rebuild militaries and economies after successive wars.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Opportunity for European defence and industrial firms in Gulf, Turkish and Pakistani modernisation.
insights.locator: The regional powers have also seen

insights.claim: In the long run the E4+R4 format could underpin a Middle East security architecture beyond the Mecca pact's deterrence model, possibly including Iran and Israel by merging the Tehran track and the Abraham Accords.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: A long-shot inclusive regional architecture would materially lower Gulf risk premia.

insights.claim: The E4 and R4 fear Washington may agree to curtail the IAEA's monitoring role in a future deal with Iran, so Europeans should make EU sanctions relief conditional on enhanced international monitoring regardless of what Washington agrees bilaterally.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: EU sanctions relief may lag any US-Iran deal, delaying European market re-entry into Iran.
insights.locator: On Iran, Europe and its regional partners

insights.claim: R4 countries could be the first to invest in Iran's post-sanctions economy, since European companies wary of reputational exposure are likely to be slower to return.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Gulf and Turkish capital would likely gain first-mover advantage in a post-sanctions Iran.
insights.locator: On Iran, Europe and its regional partners

insights.claim: Because Iran's missile and drone programme proved effective in the past year, Tehran is unlikely to negotiate a major rollback, so the E4 and R4 should instead disrupt supply chains from China and Russia and interdict shipments to Hizbullah and the Houthis.
insights.speaker: Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Expect intensified interdiction and secondary-sanction enforcement on dual-use supply chains.
insights.locator: Both the E4 and R4 view
